content.text: FacebookLog InLog InForgot Account?Physicscalculations's PostPhysicscalculationsAugust 30, 2025 · Shared with PublicWhat is an Orbit in Physics?Definition:An orbit is the curved path followed by an object under the influence of gravity as it moves around a larger body, such as a planet around the Sun or a satellite around Earth. Explanation:Orbits occur because of a balance between forward motion and gravitational pull: • Gravity pulls the object inward. • Forward velocity keeps it moving sideways. • The result is continuous free fall around the central body, instead of crashing into it.Types of Orbits:• Circular orbit → constant distance from centre.• Elliptical orbit → varying distance, with closest point = perihelion/perigee and farthest = aphelion/apogee.• Geostationary orbit → satellite appears fixed over one spot on Earth (24-hour period).Imagine:Think of swinging a stone tied to a string. The string pulls the stone inward (like gravity), while the stone’s speed keeps it moving in a circle, that’s how orbits work.In simple terms:An orbit is the path an object takes when it keeps “falling around” another object due to gravity.Formula (Orbital Velocity):v = √(GM/R)Where:• G = gravitational constant• M = mass of central body• R = distance from centreKey Points:• Caused by gravity and motion balance.• Can be circular, elliptical, or geostationary.• Natural (planets, moons) or artificial (satellites).• Essential for astronomy and space science.Examples:• Earth orbiting the Sun.• Moon orbiting Earth.• International Space Station orbiting Earth.Applications / Relevance:• Satellites.• Space exploration.• GPS and navigation.• Astronomy.• Physics education.Question:Why don’t planets fall into the Sun?Answer:Because their forward velocity keeps them in continuous orbit, they are always “falling” toward the Sun but never hitting it.#fblifestyle #physicsAll reactions:2955 comments55 sharesLikeCommentMost relevant Top fanVinod Kumar KhuranaPath followed by the satellite around planet and path followed by planet around the sun (star) is orbit32wTesfaye ChakaElliptical32wMats TrohlinThe speed of the Rotation determines hos the rotating object moves towards the center point or outwards from the center point.
